costGuide.title: Lexus 2AR-FSE Engine Replacement Cost (UK)
costGuide.labourLine: Fitting a 2AR-FSE typically takes 10-14 hours at £65-£85/hr (independent Lexus hybrid specialist) - the hybrid system adds complexity during removal and refitting .
paragraphs: What moves the price most for this engine is whether the replacement unit has had the head gasket replaced (early units) and whether the water pump and EGR cooler are fresh. A reconditioned 2AR-FSE with a documented head gasket replacement and decarbonised intake valves will command a premium - and is often worth it for the peace of mind in a premium hybrid. See our full reconditioned engine cost guide for more detail.

failures.title: Lexus 2AR-FSE Engine Problems - What Actually Fails

items.title: Head gasket failure - 2010-2013 ES300h, IS300h, GS300h
items.whatHappens: Early 2AR-FSE engines have a known susceptibility to head gasket failure, similar to the 2ZR-FXE. The gasket between cylinders 2 and 3 can develop a breach, allowing coolant to enter the combustion chamber. Symptoms include a rough cold start (misfire that clears after a few seconds), loss of coolant, and white smoke from the exhaust on start-up. If ignored, coolant contamination can damage the catalytic converter and hybrid system components.
items.repairVsReplace: A head gasket replacement on a 2AR-FSE is a significant job - typically £1,500-£2,800 at a specialist. If caught early, repair is viable. If the engine has overheated or the coolant has contaminated the oil, a reconditioned replacement engine is usually more cost-effective.

items.title: Oil consumption - piston ring wear (early 2AR-FSE)
items.whatHappens: Like many direct-injection engines, the 2AR-FSE can experience oil consumption due to worn or stuck piston rings. This is more pronounced on early units (2010-2013) and vehicles that have had extended oil change intervals. Consumption of 1 litre per 1,000 miles is not uncommon.
items.repairVsReplace: For moderate consumption, switching to a slightly thicker oil (e.g., 5W-30 instead of 0W-20) can help. Severe cases require piston ring replacement - an engine-out job that often makes a reconditioned exchange unit more economical.

items.title: Water pump and EGR cooler leaks
items.whatHappens: The electric water pump and EGR cooler on the 2AR-FSE can develop coolant leaks over time. The water pump is a known weak point; if it fails, the engine can overheat, accelerating head gasket failure. The EGR cooler can also develop internal leaks, allowing coolant to enter the intake.
items.repairVsReplace: Both components are replaceable as standalone items (£400-£800 each). Neither typically writes off the engine - but ignoring either can lead to the head gasket failure mentioned above.

failures.goodYearsLine: Post-2013 2AR-FSE units received a revised head gasket part number. Failures on 2014+ models are significantly less common, though still possible at very high mileage. Regular coolant changes (every 5 years / 50,000 miles) and using the correct 0W-20 or 5W-30 oil are the best preventative measures.

variants.title: How to Confirm You Have the 2AR-FSE
variants.intro: The 2AR-FSE is Lexus's 2.5-litre Atkinson-cycle hybrid D-4S engine, used in the ES300h, IS300h, and GS300h. The code is physically stamped on the engine block - typically on the front side of the block, just below the cylinder head, or on a machined pad near the bellhousing. Commonly confused with: - 2AR-FE - the 2.5‑litre conventional (Otto‑cycle) engine used in non‑hybrid Toyota Camry, RAV4, and the Lexus ES250 (export markets). It has port injection rather than D‑4S, and is not hybrid‑tuned. Not a straight swap. - 2AR-FXE - the 2.5‑litre Atkinson‑cycle hybrid engine used in the Toyota Camry Hybrid and Lexus NX300h. It shares the same block but has different ECU calibration, intake, and hybrid system integration - not a direct interchange without significant rework. - A25A-FXS - the newer 2.5‑litre Dynamic Force hybrid engine fitted to the 7th‑gen ES300h and current Camry Hybrid. It is a completely different engine family with higher efficiency and power - not interchangeable.

relatives.description: the 3.5‑litre V6 used in pre‑hybrid Lexus IS350 and GS350. In models like the GS, the 2AR‑FSE replaced the 2GR‑FSE for hybrid duty, offering lower fuel consumption with comparable refinement - though significantly less power.

the 2.5‑litre Dynamic Force hybrid engine introduced in the 7th‑generation ES300h (XZ10) and current Camry Hybrid. It offers significantly higher thermal efficiency (41%) and improved power output (215 hp system total), and it replaces the 2AR‑FSE in newer Lexus and Toyota hybrids. It is a completely different engine family - not a swap option.

the Atkinson‑cycle 2.5‑litre hybrid engine used in the Toyota Camry Hybrid and Lexus NX300h. It shares the same block and basic architecture but has different D‑4S calibration, intake manifold, and hybrid control logic. It is not a direct swap for the 2AR‑FSE without significant ECU rework.

buyingGuide.title: Buying a Replacement 2AR-FSE - What to Choose

options.label: Used
options.body: A used 2AR‑FSE can be a cost‑effective choice for older ES300h/IS300h values, provided the donor has documented service history. The key checks are: (1) has the head gasket been replaced (especially on 2010-2013 units)? (2) does the engine have a recent water pump? A used unit with a documented head gasket replacement and less than 80,000 miles offers excellent value. Link once: [used engines service]

options.label: Reconditioned
options.body: A properly reconditioned 2AR‑FSE should include a new head gasket (preferably the revised post‑2013 part number), new piston rings (to address oil consumption), a new water pump, and a full top‑end gasket set. The timing chain is rarely an issue, but a thorough inspection is standard. This is the sweet spot for owners - you get a like‑new engine with the known weaknesses addressed, at a fraction of the cost of a new unit from Lexus. Reconditioned units typically come with a 12-24 month warranty. Link once: [reconditioned engines service]

options.label: Rebuilt
options.body: A full rebuild is only justified for low‑mileage, cherished vehicles (e.g. a clean‑car IS300h with low chassis miles). A quality rebuild will include bottom‑end bearings, piston rings, valve guides, seals, and a full timing system refresh. This is the most expensive option but offers the closest thing to a new engine. Link once: [rebuilt engines service]

buyingGuide.supplyFitLine: All options above can be supplied and fitted through our network of vetted UK Lexus and Toyota specialists. Each quote includes warranty details and delivery options. Link once: [supply and fit service]
buyingGuide.vehicleValueNote: The 2AR‑FSE sits in vehicles worth £6,000-£18,000 depending on year and mileage (ES300h, IS300h). A reconditioned engine at £2,200-£3,800 represents roughly 20-40% of the car's value - which is a justifiable investment for a premium hybrid that, once refreshed, will outlast the chassis. For a higher‑mileage IS300h worth under £6,000, a used engine with a solid warranty is often the most sensible financial choice. Always factor in the condition of the hybrid battery and gearbox before committing to an expensive reconditioned engine.

items.question: Should I buy a used or reconditioned 2AR‑FSE?
items.answer: For lower‑value vehicles (e.g. an older IS300h under £6,000), a used engine with a solid warranty is often the most sensible choice, provided the donor has documented history and a recent head gasket replacement (if pre‑2013). For cars worth £8,000+, a reconditioned unit is the sweet spot - it comes with a new head gasket (revised part), new piston rings, fresh water pump, and a 12‑24 month warranty. items.answer: The engine code is stamped on the block (typically on the front side, just below the cylinder head) and is also on your V5C under “Engine number”. Alternatively, enter your registration above and we'll confirm your exact fitment. Check your engine via registration
bullets: Don’t confuse it with the 2AR‑FE (non‑hybrid, port‑injected) or the 2AR‑FXE (different hybrid calibration) - they are not interchangeable.
If your ES, IS, or GS is a hybrid with a 2.5‑litre petrol engine, it’s almost certainly the 2AR‑FSE.

items.question: How long does a 2AR‑FSE engine typically last?
items.answer: With proper maintenance, the 2AR‑FSE can exceed 200,000 miles. The engine is chain‑driven, so no timing belt replacement is needed. Regular oil changes (every 10,000 miles or 12 months) and coolant flushes (every 5 years) are critical to head gasket and water pump longevity. Many UK Lexus hybrids have clocked 200,000+ miles on the original engine. The early head gasket issue is a known risk, but once addressed with a revised gasket, the engine is extremely durable. A reconditioned unit, when fitted properly, should provide another 150,000+ miles of reliable service.
